# CM24: Sun's CM−24 curve, the halfpoint, and the surviving Hasse binding

2026-10-15. Bounded paper/source binding only. Canonical owner
EM-DIRECT-18F24A and support EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D are unchanged.
Root requested the exact geometric binding and highlighted the nonsplit
coefficient-field issue; the support author checked the formulas below.
No independent formal review or p² connection theorem is claimed.

## Readset and reuse

The old halfpoint literature memo, lines51–62, already records the
CM−24 label, matching degree/argument and excluded prime classes. These
are REUSED, not new results. Its exact file is
`CM24_COMPLEMENT_LEGENDRE_HALFPOINT_BOUNDED_LITERATURE_MEMO_20261015.md`,
5123B, SHA25682411aeae62efe66d5e0076e5084be169a13ba66a0f61275750378783b992766.
The four-source parameter memo does not supply the missing coefficients.

Only the already selected primary paper was reopened:
Zhi-Hong Sun, *Congruences involving binom(2k,k)² binom(3k,k) m^(−k)*,
arXiv1104.2789v3,28Apr2011,
[versioned primary PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1104.2789v3).
Locators: Theorem3.1, printed p.5; Corollary3.1,p.8;
Lemma4.1,p.12; Lemma4.6 and Theorem4.5,p.19; their proof and
Conjecture4.1,p.20. PDF page indices are respectively4,7,11,18,19.
Sun's [I] is N.Ishii, *Trace of Frobenius endomorphism of an elliptic
curve with complex multiplication*, Bull.Austral.Math.Soc.70(2004),
125–142. Sun points to its p.133 and Theorem3.1. No Ishii read was
needed: Sun supplies the curve coefficients required here. No additional
paper/search or claimed explicit CM endomorphism is imported.

## The models and coordinate/differential normalization

Put u²=2 over K=Q(u), t=u/2=1/u, delta=1+u. Sun's two models are

    E_t: Y²=f_t(X)=X³+3(4t−5)X+2(2t²−14t+11),
    E_I: Y²=X³+(−21+12u)X−28+22u.                  (1)

Lemma4.6 identifies E_I as having CM by the order of discriminant−24.
This CM-order discriminant is distinct from a Weierstrass discriminant.
At t=±u/2 the coefficient pairs are

    E_+: (A_+,B_+)=(−15+6u,24−14u),
    E_-: (A_-,B_-)=(−15−6u,24+14u).                 (2)

The halfpoint is the FAMILY PARAMETER t, not a specified elliptic
point (X,Y). Our original zeta²=1/2 may be bound by u=2zeta.
The already saved S(zeta)=−zeta and even n make the sign harmless
for the Legendre VALUE; this is not a new period/class identification.

Here is explicit paper algebra fixing the twist convention:

    delta²(−21+12u)=−15−6u,
    delta³(−28+22u)=24+14u.                         (3)

Thus E_- is the delta quadratic twist of E_I, not a silently identical
Weierstrass model. If eta²=delta, the map
`(X,Y) -> (delta X,eta³Y)` gives E_I -> E_- over K(eta).
With omega= dX/(2Y) on each displayed model its pullback is
`omega_- -> eta^(−1) omega_I`. Conjugating(3) gives the analogous
map from the conjugate of E_I to E_+. No particular square root of
delta is chosen over a residue field without checking its existence.

For clarity the invariants were expanded directly from(1), not
inferred from the project name:

    Delta_W(E_t)=6912(1−t)(1+t)³,
    j(E_t)=432(5−4t)³/[(1−t)(1+t)³],
    Delta_W(E_I)=1728(577−408u)=1728 delta^(−8),
    Delta_W(E_+)=1728(3+2u)=1728 delta²,
    Delta_W(E_-)=1728(3−2u)=1728 delta^(−2),
    j(E_I)=j(E_-)=1728(1399+988u),
    j(E_+)=1728(1399−988u).                         (4)

For example 4A_I³+27B_I²=−108(577−408u), and
577−408u=(u−1)^8=delta^(−8). These discriminants are units at
every p>3 because delta has norm−1. All original primes are covered.
The fixed omega spans the Hodge line; no full de Rham/Frobenius basis,
crystalline matrix or original target-relative class has been chosen.

## Exact mod-p factor, and when it is actually a trace

Write chi_3=(p/3)=(−3/p), not (3/p), l=(p−1)/2, and

    h_p(E_t,omega_t)=[X^(p−1)] f_t(X)^l.             (5)

Theorem3.1 is an Fp-character-sum statement. Corollary3.1 supplies
the stronger VARIABLE polynomial congruence

    P_floor(p/3)(t)=−chi_3 sum_(x in Fp) f_t(x)^l
                  = chi_3 h_p(E_t,omega_t) modp.    (6)

The last equality follows directly from finite-field power sums:
deg_X f_t^l=3l<2(p−1), so the only positive multiple of p−1 is
p−1; the constant contribution sums to p=0. This proof is valid
after extension of the coefficient field. Thus(6) is legitimate at
t=zeta in Fp². It records the Hasse coefficient with the displayed
Weierstrass differential, not a characteristic-zero period value.

If t belongs to Fp, point counting gives
`a_p(E_t)=−sum_(x in Fp) chi_p(f_t(x))`, hence

    P_floor(p/3)(t)=chi_3 a_p(E_t) modp.              (7)

For E_- versus E_I the twist factors, with no normalization suppressed,
are `a_p(E_-)=chi_p(delta)a_p(E_I)` when all data lie in Fp, and

    h_p(E_-,omega_-)=delta^l h_p(E_I,omega_I)         (8)

over any characteristic-p coefficient extension. To check(8), substitute
X=delta Z in the twisted cubic: its l-th power acquires delta^(3l),
whereas coefficient extraction contributes delta^(p−1)=delta^(2l).
In Fp, delta^l reduces to the quadratic character used in Lemma4.1.
Over Fp² it must not be replaced by that Fp sign.

For reference, on Sun's stated split-coefficient domain p≡±1mod8,
put p=a²+6b² when p≡1,7mod24. Lemma4.6 uses the exact integer sums

    sum chi_p(f_I)=2a(2a/3) chi_p(delta),
    sum chi_p(f_+)=2a(2a/3),                         (9)

and zero sums for p≡17,23mod24. Consequently Theorem4.5 gives
`P_floor(p/3)(u/2)=2a(a/3) modp` in the first cases and zero in
the latter cases. These are the actual sign/twist conventions in
that version, not a p² divided-difference formula.

## What survives for the original two prime classes

Here p=6m+1≡13,19mod24, n=2m=floor(p/3), d=4m. Therefore

    chi_3=1, (2/p)=−1, zeta^p=−zeta,
    K modp = Fp², E_zeta^(p)=E_(−zeta).             (10)

E_zeta is not a curve over Fp in this displayed model. Its two
j-invariants in(4) are conjugate; coefficient conjugation and the
relative p-Frobenius carry E_zeta to E_(−zeta), rather than giving
a p-Frobenius self-endomorphism of this one model. An actual
Fp²-point-count trace is `a_(p²)=p²+1−#E_zeta(Fp²)`; it is neither
the sum over x in Fp in(6) nor an Fp trace a_p from(7).

Nevertheless the valid polynomial identity(6) yields exactly

    P_(2m)(zeta)=h_p(E_zeta,omega_zeta) modp,
    h_p(E_(−zeta),omega_(−zeta))
        =h_p(E_zeta,omega_zeta),                    (11)

the second equality using the evenness of P_(2m). This is the
surviving basis-bound identity. Any already proved mod-p vanishing
may be reused in(11), but Sun's Lemma4.6/Theorem4.5 are NOT proofs
for these two classes: both require p≡1,7mod8. In the read version
the corresponding halfpoint zero is instead stated as Conjecture4.1;
no assertion about its present literature status is made here.

No explicit E_zeta -> E_(−zeta) isogeny, its differential multiplier,
or normalized semilinear comparison was given in these inspected
passages. The twist(3) connects a DIFFERENT CM model to E_-, not
those two conjugate models directly. A specific conjugate-curve map
with its differential normalization is a precise further object one
could construct; its absence from this readset is not an impossibility
or an environmental/permission obstruction. No such construction is
started in this binding step.

## Delivered scope and remaining input

The added data are(1)–(4), the precise trace/twist factors(6)–(9),
and the distinction(10)–(11) that keeps the original nonsplit classes
inside a valid mod-p Hasse statement. These supplement, rather than
repackage, the old applicability memo. Neither(6) nor a mod-p zero
retains `(P_(4m)(zeta)−P_(2m)(zeta))/(3p) modp`. That numerator
still must be formed over the p-integral lift before division; no
unsquared p² value or lift normalization is provided here. A further
map to the full weighted ell(T)=3Y functional, including H_b and the
quarter contribution, is independently unproved. R endpoint, Y/Z/kappa
and all original parent goals remain OPEN.

Only one prior primary paper was reopened, with bounded local memo
dedup and paper arithmetic. No scientific code/prime/sample/checker/
Hart/solve, new Task/claim/owner, remote Source/RA/Native/STATE/VIEW
or successor. P000/Heartbeat X6 external-arithmetic typing is unchanged.
This single geometric binding step ends with this local note.

# Explicit three-isogeny and its differential-basis candidate

2026-10-15 UTC. Root EM-DVR-FBF223 author-side paper derivation for the
unchanged owner EM-DIRECT-18F24A and support EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D.
Candidate pending source matching and separate checking; not Native
acceptance, not a completed CM/period/target bridge. No science program,
sample, checker, symbolic computation or new owner is used.

## Curve and normalized quotient

Over a characteristic-zero coefficient field, or good characteristic>3,
consider the specific candidate family

    E_t: y^2=f_t(x)=x^3+A_t x+B_t,
    A_t=3(4t-5), B_t=2(2t^2-14t+11).

Its discriminant is

    Delta_t=6912(1-t)(1+t)^3.

Thus t!=+/-1 is nonsingular. The point Q=(3,2(t+1)) is on E_t;
its tangent has slope3, so [2]Q=-Q and it has exact order3.
Put z=x-3, c=12(t+1), b=2(t+1). Then

    f_t(x)=z^3+9z^2+c z+b^2.

The normalized Velu quotient by {O,+/-Q} has the rational candidate

    X=x+2c/z+4b^2/z^2,
    Y=y*(1-2c/z^2-8b^2/z^3),
    E'_t: Y^2=X^3+A'_t X+B'_t,
    A'_t=-27(4t+5)=9 A_(-t),
    B'_t=-54(2t^2+14t+11)=-27 B_(-t).

The X expression follows directly by adding x(P+Q)-x(Q) and
x(P-Q)-x(Q) to x(P). The Y expression is y*dX/dx, the normalized
differential rule. The standard short Weierstrass quotient coefficients
give A'=A-10(27+A), B'=B-14(135+9A+2B), yielding the expressions above.
These identities can be checked by ordinary paper polynomial algebra.

Choose u with u^2=-3. The isomorphism E'_t -> E_(-t) is

    (X,Y) -> (X/u^2,Y/u^3).

Its composition j_t:E_t -> E_(-t) is a concrete degree3 isogeny.
No relation to the scientific source is claimed before the support
checks the family's exact coefficients, twist factor and normalization.

## Exact differential reduction

Use omega_t=dx/(2y), eta_t=x dx/(2y), and the corresponding primed
basis. The normalized quotient phi_t satisfies

    phi_t^* omega'_t=omega_t,
    phi_t^* eta'_t=3eta_t-6omega_t-2d(y/(x-3)).

Indeed direct differentiation gives

    d(y/z)=[z-c/z-2b^2/z^2]omega_t.

So (X-x)omega_t=-2d(y/z)+2(x-3)omega_t, proving the reduction.
The exact term is retained as a rational differential; this is equality
of algebraic de Rham classes, not a pointwise period evaluation.
The isomorphism to E_(-t) pulls omega_(-t) to u omega'_t and
eta_(-t) to u^-1 eta'_t. Therefore the proposed matrix, with columns
the pullbacks of omega_(-t),eta_(-t) in basis omega_t,eta_t, is

    J=u [[1,2],[0,-1]],
    det J=3, J^2=-3 I.

It is independent of t in these exact bases. This basis statement
does not on its own identify the earlier rank2 Legendre solution
matrix with geometric de Rham cohomology.

## Original halfpoint and field issue

At t=zeta, zeta^2=1/2, the j-invariant reduces algebraically to

    j(E_zeta)=2417472-3414528*zeta
             =2417472-1707264*sqrt(2).

The conjugate j is obtained at -zeta; their sum is4834944 and their
product is14670139392. Matching these with CM discriminant-24 still
requires an actual cited CM identification, not a label-based inference.

For the original primes p=13 or19 mod24, (2/p)=-1 and (-3/p)=1.
Thus zeta lies in F_(p^2), zeta^p=-zeta, while u may be chosen in F_p.
The p-power relative Frobenius is E_zeta -> E_(-zeta), rather than
an E_zeta self-map. The explicit j_(-zeta) can return the conjugate
curve to E_zeta. Its differential-basis matrix is specified above;
Frobenius must still be treated semilinearly. No F_p character-sum
trace theorem is extended to these nonsplit parameters by fiat.

This candidate supplies neither a mod-p^2 geometric Frobenius matrix
nor a p-integral comparison to the finite P_n/P_d sections, nor their
unsquared divided endpoint difference, nor the relative functional
ell(T)=3Y. All those source-specific identifications remain OPEN.
The existing finite spectral originals and reviews are unchanged.

The map is a standard three-torsion quotient specialized to a concrete
family; global novelty is not claimed. Its possible value here is the
explicit conjugate-curve and exact differential normalization data.

In the column convention where period vector (w,e) obeys w'=alpha w+beta e, e'=gamma w-alpha e, elimination gives beta'/beta=-2t/(t^2-1), alpha'+alpha^2+beta gamma-alpha beta'/beta =-2/[9(t^2-1)], (1-t^2)w''-2t w'-(2/9)w=0. Over z=(1-t)/2, the formal normalized geometric hypergeometric solution is sum_(j>=0) (1/3)_j(2/3)_j z^j/(j!)^2. For j

=p, integral infinite series, evaluation at a unit, analytic/crystalline period normalization, or complete endpoint value is supplied by this finite-prefix statement. There is no inference that substituting z=(1-zeta)/2 in a discarded infinite tail is legal. This proposed exact geometric connection and finite-prefix comparison do not provide the geometric Frobenius matrix, the divided endpoint value R(zeta), its first jet, or identification with ell(T)=3Y. members.utf8_content: # Fixed source geometry: three-isogeny, de Rham basis and Legendre operator 2026-10-15. Author-side bounded paper unit, original scientific owner EM-DIRECT-18F24A; support EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D. Root EM-DVR-FBF223 supplied the map and differential-matrix candidate, derived before saving its direction file. Root is a mathematical coauthor, not an independent decisive reviewer. Shared-context support checking is not formal independent review. This paper awaits Root's separate review dispatch; it does not extend any prior PASS. ## Fixed input, dedup, and coefficient ring This checks the 4041B Root candidate `control/ROOT_CM24_EXPLICIT_THREE_ISOGENY_AND_DIFFERENTIAL_BASIS_CANDIDATE_20261015.md`, SHA25698d593c1085f7e95498b49fd19a342be9040b992a9660ac25f3f40c845d810d7. Its coefficients match the just-frozen 8493B source-binding note, SHA256b6e1a70b2d77824656fe28128e5b3c96be9ea0755b0c0ef2c3379cdab2aa7e05. That note records the exact Sun1104.2789v3 loci. Prior notes established only the twist from the CM model and a mod-p Hasse coefficient identity, not this explicit conjugate-curve map or its whole differential matrix. Those source facts are reused. Neither prior note is modified. Before this proof was frozen, Root additionally supplied the fixed 3708B candidate `control/ROOT_CM24_GEOMETRIC_GAUSS_MANIN_TO_FIXED_LEGENDRE_CANDIDATE_20261015.md`, SHA2563ae1254b059deb5cf16bb90dfed670a61d44620e83fee85a8d5dcb02ff5cff0f. Its exact connection and finite-prefix claims are checked below in this same bounded geometry unit, with Root's authorship disclosed. To prevent the two square roots from being conflated, write beta²=2, nu²=−3, A_t=3(4t−5), B_t=2(2t²−14t+11), E_t: y²=x³+A_t x+B_t, omega_t=dx/(2y), eta_t=x dx/(2y). (1) The fixed base is B=Z[1/6,t,(1−t²)^(-1),nu]/(nu²+3). (2) Thus E_t and E_(−t) are smooth proper elliptic curves with origins at infinity: their displayed discriminants are 6912(1−t)(1+t)³ and 6912(1+t)(1−t)³. In particular 2,3,nu and t±1 are units. The proofs are rational polynomial/differential identities over(2) and specialize to all original residue characteristics, not to selected examples. All checks here occurred after reading the fixed Root candidate; no blind or platform-certified preregistration is claimed. ## The degree-three map, with a complete finite identity Let b=2(t+1), c=12(t+1)=6b, z=x−3. Then y²=z³+9z²+cz+b², Q=(3,b), y²−(b+3z)²=z³. (3) Since b is a unit, Q and −Q are distinct, neither is the origin. The line y=b+3z has triple intersection at Q, so Q has exact order3. Define on the complement of z=0 X=x+2c/z+4b²/z², Y=y(1−2c/z²−8b²/z³), A_q=−27(4t+5)=9A_(−t), B_q=−54(2t²+14t+11)=−27B_(−t). (4) Here is a complete cleared polynomial identity verifying its image, without depending on a numerical check or an unspecified quotient formula. Put e=b² and f=z³+9z²+cz+e, M=z³−2cz−8e, N=z³+3z²+2cz+4e, A_q=−9c−27, B_q=54−45c−27e. Ordinary multiplication gives f M²−N³−A_q N z⁴−B_q z⁶ =2z²(c²−36e)(3z³−2cz−6e)=0. (5) For reproducibility the only possibly nonzero difference coefficients before c²=36e are imposed are: z⁵, 6(c²−36e); z³, −4c(c²−36e); z², −12e(c²−36e). Since X=N/z² and Y=yM/z³, (5) proves Y²=X³+A_q X+B_q exactly. One also obtains X directly by summing the x-coordinate corrections from addition by Q and −Q. The normalized Y in(4) satisfies Y=y dX/dx, so for the displayed quotient curve E_q, phi_t^* omega_q=omega_t. (6) At Q and −Q, X and Y have poles of orders2 and3 respectively, with leading terms 4b²/z² and ∓8b³/z³. They therefore extend to the origin on E_q. At the original origin X~x,Y~y, so the map also sends origin to origin and extends to the complete curves. The pole divisor of X is exactly2(O+Q+(−Q)); no cancellation occurs because b is a unit. As x on E_q has pole divisor2O_q, deg phi_t=3 and its origin fiber consists of those three points. A morphism between elliptic curves carrying origin to origin is a group homomorphism. Its nonzero invariant-differential pullback(6) also verifies separability. These facts prove the claimed normalized three-isogeny, including its kernel, rather than merely a relation between two j-invariants. The coefficient scaling in(4), and nu⁶=−27, give an isomorphism k_t:E_q -> E_(−t), (X,Y) -> (X/nu²,Y/nu³). Consequently j_t=k_t o phi_t is the fixed degree-three isogeny E_t -> E_(−t). No symbol beta=√2 is used for this scaling. ## Literal differential identities and the cohomology matrix The normalized quotient has the following equality of rational differential FORMS, with its exact term retained: d(y/z)=[z−c/z−2b²/z²] omega_t, phi_t^* eta_q=3eta_t−6omega_t−2d(y/z). (7) Indeed differentiation of y²=f gives the first formula as `(f'/z−2f/z²)omega_t`; the second follows from `X−x=2(x−3)−2[z−c/z−2b²/z²]`. No integration or division by p is involved. Scaling to the conjugate curve then gives j_t^* omega_(−t)=nu omega_t, j_t^* eta_(−t)=2nu omega_t−nu eta_t −(2/nu)d(y/z). (8) For smooth proper de Rham cohomology over(2), the usual Weierstrass classes of omega_t and the second-kind differential eta_t form the specified rank-two basis. Equation(8) gives, with columns equal to the pullbacks of the TARGET basis in the SOURCE basis, (j_t^*omega_(−t),j_t^*eta_(−t)) =(omega_t,eta_t) J in de Rham classes, J=nu [[1,2],[0,−1]], det J=3, J²=−3 I. (9) The sign of the chosen nu changes the selected map by target negation; fixing nu is therefore part of the normalization. Replacing t by −t does not alter J with that same choice. The last square in(9) is a matrix statement; no additional equality of composed elliptic maps is inferred solely from their differentials. For period COLUMN vectors paired along corresponding cycles, the matrix is the transpose, consistently with that column-of-classes convention: period-column pullback map = J^T. (10) The notation “in de Rham classes” matters. The function y/z has poles at O,Q,−Q. Its exact differential in(7)–(8) is accounted for by a rational/Čech representative with these finite principal parts; it is not a globally regular form being silently discarded. The primitive has only simple poles, the derivative double poles, and the identities use only denominators2,3 and the coefficient units. They persist over B and modulo p² for p>3 without a char-p integration assertion or loss of a Frobenius kernel. For a relative class or an actual endpoint integral the rational-function boundary term must be retained unless separately proved to cancel. In particular(9) is p-integral and invertible in every original characteristic because det J=3 is a unit. This prime-to-p isogeny matrix is distinct from a degree-p Frobenius comparison with determinant divisible by p. ## Exact Gauss–Manin reduction and the fixed Legendre operator For this section only, put a=A_t,b=B_t and D=4a³+27b²; the earlier kernel-point constant b=2(t+1) is no longer used here. # CM24 source geometry, three-isogeny and fixed Legendre module: bounded review

2026-10-15 UTC. Reviewer EM-NONAUTHOR-5DF3A9B6, retaining own contribution identity EM-DVR-03A554. Directed shared-context NONBLIND local mathematical review, not a Native DR, Task verdict, crystalline certification or new scientific ownership action.

**Verdict: bounded PASS, with one nonblocking cross-reference correction and no mandatory mathematical correction.** The fixed package supplies the source-bound curve/Hasse normalization, a degree-three conjugate-curve isogeny with its integral de Rham matrix, the geometric Gauss–Manin connection and its unit first-jet change to L_*, and the stated finite-prefix comparison with Qstar. It does not supply a geometric Frobenius matrix/initial value, complete unit-point period, divided endpoint value or original relative-functional Y bridge. Prior comparison/spectral PASS judgments are reused only at their stated inputs, not extended automatically to this package.

## Exact inputs and independence

The main fixed targets under `/workspace/em-research-continuation-20261014/cm24-connection/` are:

1. `CM24_EXPLICIT_CONJUGATE_THREE_ISOGENY_AND_INTEGRAL_DR_BASIS_20261015.md`: 13,972 bytes, SHA-256 `929e5b4364c846dacce8897f6e4aed0bd822a3e7b3b3d073f11e9594d5239305`, Git blob `288057285a2f5ab50543da0f77a007736441c948`.
2. `CM24_SOURCE_GEOMETRY_THREE_ISOGENY_AND_FIXED_LEGENDRE_FINAL_FROZEN_MANIFEST_20261015.json`: 6,074 bytes, SHA-256 `b02fb2423310661791f85e24132a30681cf63cffd834aacfe7d4ade5b92891e4`, Git blob `9e874205c247471e987d96b6f5033d23331d261e`.

The manifest's four members, together with itself, are exactly five input originals totaling 36,288 bytes. I read all five, including the unchanged 8,493-byte Sun/curve note and Root's 4,041/3,708-byte candidates. The companion fullpin records their actual complete local byte/SHA/blob checks and minimal prior references.

Canonical owner EM-DIRECT-18F24A and support author EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D remain unchanged. Root EM-DVR-FBF223 contributed the map, differential matrix and geometric-connection candidates and is a real coauthor, not an independent reviewer. Their author-side support is not decisive acceptance. I retain prior CM24/Source/control exposure and the disclosed read-only preparation on these candidates; I do not claim blind or platform-attested independence. None of these author identities is mine. The author incorporated the new GM candidate before freezing the final combined proof; I waited for those final bytes before giving this combined verdict.

One temporary reviewer-side read-only sanity check, `/root/math_nonauthor_review/sampler_proof_sanity`, read only the final main manuscript and found no blocking issue. It performed no scientific code/sample, file write, network/Native action or scientific ownership/claim. It did not verify Source applicability and is not an additional Native DR. I independently checked the algebra, source and scope and give the judgment here. Both reviewer-side and author-side checking are disclosed rather than described as clean/blind review.

## 1. Primary-source and coefficient-field binding

I directly reopened only [Sun's versioned primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1104.2789v3), at Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.1, Lemmas 4.1/4.6, Theorem 4.5 and Conjecture 4.1. Corollary 3.1 explicitly concerns a variable t; its proof uses degree at most p-1 to pass from F_p values to a polynomial identity. The stated curve coefficients and factor `(p/3)=(-3/p)` agree. Finite-field power sums then yield the Hasse coefficient after any coefficient-field extension. The CM model/label and split-prime theorem domain also agree with the note; that theorem does not cover the original nonsplit classes. No present-day conjecture-status or extra Ishii-paper claim is imported.

The note's coordinate and twist checks are valid: delta=1+sqrt(2) scales the displayed CM model to E_minus with coefficient factors delta²/delta³, while an isomorphism after adjoining its square root pulls the invariant differential back with the inverse square-root factor. Its expanded discriminants and conjugate j-invariants match the curves; delta has norm -1, giving good reduction for the original p>3. The parameter halfpoint is not an elliptic endpoint or a chosen cycle.

The Hasse scalar uses exactly `omega=dx/(2y)` and the coefficient of X^(p-1) in f^((p-1)/2). The twist factor is delta^((p-1)/2), not automatically an F_p character over F_p². For p congruent to 13 or 19 modulo 24, sqrt(2) is nonsplit but sqrt(-3) is split. Thus the extension-field Hasse assertion is valid; an F_p point-count trace for that one displayed F_p² model is not being asserted. The two square roots beta and nu and the separate coefficient beta_c are correctly distinguished in the final proof.

## 2. Cleared map identity, extension, degree and kernel

On the fixed smooth base with 6 and 1-t² inverted, the point Q has b=2(t+1) a unit. The identity `y²-(b+3z)²=z³` proves a triple tangent intersection at Q. Hence Q is nonzero of exact order three and Q,-Q,O are distinct sections.

I checked the complete map identity, not only the invariant differential. Expanding fM² and `N³+A_q N z⁴+B_q z⁶` with c,e independent cancels every coefficient except

`z⁵: 6(c²-36e)`,
`z³: -4c(c²-36e)`,
`z²: -12e(c²-36e)`.

These are exactly the factorization in (5) and vanish because c=6b,e=b². Together with X=N/z² and Y=yM/z³ this proves the claimed target equation. The target's coefficient scaling by nu²/nu³ is correct, with nu²=-3 and nu⁶=-27.

At Q and -Q, z is a local parameter since 2y=+/-2b is a unit. The nonzero leading pole coefficients give orders two and three for X,Y. At O they have the original x,y leading terms. Thus the rational map extends to the complete curves, carries those three points to the target origin and has no other pole of X. Its X pole divisor has degree six; the target x coordinate has degree two, proving map degree three. Origin preservation gives the elliptic group homomorphism, with precisely the stated kernel. Its invariant-differential pullback is nonzero (and degree three is prime to all allowed characteristics), confirming separability. This is a map/kernel proof, not just matching j-invariants or assuming the map from `Y=y X'`.

## 3. Integral de Rham classes and exact terms

The literal differentiation of y/z gives (7), including its factor of omega=dx/(2y). Pullback of eta_q is therefore `3eta-6omega-2d(y/z)`. Scaling to E_minus gives

`j^*omega_minus=nu omega`,
`j^*eta_minus=2nu omega-nu eta-(2/nu)d(y/z)`.

All coefficients and signs are correct. In source-basis coordinates the columns are consequently `nu(1,0)^T` and `nu(2,-1)^T`, yielding J, det J=3 and J²=-3I as stated. Period columns along corresponding pushed cycles transform by J^T. These column/transpose conventions are consistent; they do not supply period values or an equality of composed elliptic maps solely from a matrix square.

The integral class statement needs the proper de Rham/Čech reading used in the manuscript. On a smooth short Weierstrass model with 6 and discriminant inverted, omega and eta are the standard rank-two integral de Rham basis. At infinity eta has a double pole with a simple-pole primitive for its principal part, giving its nontrivial Čech representative; it is not a globally regular differential. The cup/residue pairing with omega is a unit, so this basis does not require an ordinary/Hasse-nonzero fiber.

The explicitly retained y/z primitive has only simple poles at O,Q,-Q; its derivative has double poles and can be accounted for by those finite principal parts. The exact reductions use units 2,3,nu,b, with no division by p or characteristic-p antiderivative. They therefore persist on the stated base and modulo p². This is sufficient for the proper cohomology-class equality. It is not a license to discard the same rational-function boundary in a relative integral or original target endpoint computation.

## 4. Exact geometric connection, jet basis and reflection

With the GM section's separately scoped a,b, the polynomial identities (13) check every coefficient in both reductions (12). In particular the omega difference has degree-four numerator whose x and constant rows give the first two identities in (13); the eta reduction also uses `(a'+4a alpha)/6=b beta_c`. There is no missing scalar normalization or period used to fit the connection. The rational primitives V/y again have only low-order principal parts, making the same integral Čech interpretation legitimate.

Substitution gives exactly

`alpha=-(2t-1)/(6(t²-1))`,
`beta_c=-1/(6(t²-1))`,
`gamma=-(4t-5)/(6(t²-1))`.

Elimination from the period differential system gives the beta_c logarithmic derivative and scalar coefficient in (15), hence precisely L_* with eigenvalue -2/9. It does not give the old L_n with its p-small eigenvalue shift. The first-jet matrix has inverse over the stated base because beta_c has inverse `-6(t²-1)`. At the halfpoint beta_c=1/3 is a unit.

The class-connection matrix is C(t), while the period-column system is its transpose. Direct checking gives `C(t)J+J C(-t)=0`; the second sign comes from the parameter reflection. In the scalar class basis `(omega,nabla_t omega)`, the identities beta_c(-t)=beta_c(t) and `alpha(-t)+2beta_c(t)=-alpha(t)` give `nu diag(1,-1)`. This is the correct reflection convention and is not a Frobenius normalization.

## 5. Finite-prefix comparison and the surviving tail

The previously reviewed Qstar theorem is used as an input, not rerun. Its affine variable change preserves degree d<p. Around z_h=(1-t)/2, the displayed normalized L_* recurrence has unit divisors j² for 1<=j<p, so it uniquely fixes that finite coefficient prefix from a_0=1. Qstar therefore has those same coefficients modulo p², including the zero coefficients for d<j<p.

This normalization is for a scalar formal solution at the singular boundary t=1; no actual geometric cycle/period value is identified by assigning its constant one. No recurrence denominator at j=p is a unit. For the hypergeometric coefficient a_p (not a curve's Frobenius trace), `(1/3)_p` and `(2/3)_p` each have exactly one p factor in the original family, while `(p!)²` has exactly two. Thus a_p is a p-unit. At the unit z_h corresponding to zeta this term has no smallness forced by valuation. This supports precisely the warning against dropping the tail; it proves neither convergence nor a total value of that infinite series and does not control every later coefficient.

## 6. Nonsplit specialization and remaining mathematical scope

The halfpoint is smooth and both nu and the relevant denominators are units. At a p-adic completion, a chosen root nu of -3 lifts in Z_p; beta generates the unramified quadratic extension. Its coefficient Frobenius sends zeta to -zeta and fixes nu. The explicit conjugate-curve isogenies therefore coexist with the relative p-Frobenius without identifying it with either degree-three map. The composition to a self-map has degree 3p, but J alone gives no missing Frobenius factor, trace or initial matrix. The old L_n comparison is not retroactively geometric Frobenius for L_*.

The ambient raw-coordinate-power lift modulo p² is also distinct from this coefficient automorphism. A family parameter halfpoint does not choose endpoints/cycles realizing the weighted original relative functional. No R(zeta), unsquared complementary difference, full endpoint jet, ell(T)=3Y value, cost gain or global no-go follows from these constructions. Full H_b and the quarter contribution remain in that separate target, and the rational exact terms cannot be dropped there. All original goals and ownership remain OPEN/unchanged.

Nonblocking editorial item: main manuscript line 274 refers to sigma “in (10)”; its intended coefficient automorphism is (18), whereas (10) is the period transpose. The formulas and scope are unambiguous. This does not require reopening the mathematics or changing the frozen bytes for this review.
